 The Wheels Are Falling Off At Porsche According To Latest Recall
 by 
 AutoGuide.com News Staff 
 (IC: employee) 
 Published:  October 23rd, 2026 
 Share 
 Porsche is expanding an existing safety recall for its highest-performing sports cars due to defective center-lock wheel nuts that can fracture and cause a wheel to detach while driving.
 Because an unsecured wheel presents an immediate crash hazard, Porsche is explicitly advising owners of affected vehicles not to drive their cars until authorized repairs are completed.
 The filing expands upon a previous recall campaign (NHTSA recall number 24V809 ) originally reported in October 2024 . The expansion adds more Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) from model year 2024 sports cars equipped with center-locking wheel systems.
 The recall adds 548 cars to the original 1,851 recalled across the following 2024 models:
 Porsche 911 GT3 and 911 GT3 RS
 Porsche 911 Turbo and 911 Turbo S
 Porsche 911 S/T
 Porsche 911 Carrera GTS
 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS
 Porsche 718 Spyder RS
 VINs involved in this expanded recall population became searchable on NHTSA.gov on October 20, 2026.

 The decision to broaden the recall comes after Porsche learned of two additional field incidents in May and August 2026 involving fractured center lock hardware. While no injuries or accidents occurred, the failures prompted Porsche and its supplier to reopen their investigation.
 Subsequent supply-chain reviews revealed previously unidentified material movements within the supplier's manufacturing and logistics facilities. These unrecorded parts transfers meant that additional center lock components—outside the original scope identified in 2024—were actually produced in the same out-of-specification manufacturing batch.
 To resolve the issue, Porsche dealers will inspect the center lock wheel fastening assemblies and replace any defective or improperly manufactured components with corrected parts free of charge. Owner notification letters are scheduled to be mailed out on December 15, 2026.
